recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). ## Roles and lifetimes in the request (approved 2026-10-29)

Decided by Kenneth in the side session "Chat history cache handoff" (`local_97f342dd-4367-4bc5-830d-1c6d6d91db47`), relayed to this doc; his words: "ok. go with your proposal." The provider-doc citations below are that session's, not re-verified here.

**Append-only record, separate from visibility.** Each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent to the model. A request renders that record plus the new items. No item is rewritten, dropped or re-derived; what the model should still see is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. Source cited: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages doc (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`): a cleared message stays in the array but renders nothing, must be re-sent verbatim, and rebuilding or dropping it counts as an edit to an earlier message that fails the thinking check and breaks the cache.

**Three roles, assigned by who speaks, never by lifetime:**

| Role | Wire | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| Operator, standing | Anthropic top-level `system`; Responses `instructions` | Standing prompt and tools, written once per chat, never changed |
| Operator, in conversation | Anthropic in-array `role:"system"` (Opus 5.5 and 5.x, not Sonnet 5); OpenAI `developer` item | Situational instructions (skills; the file-load reminder if it survives D4) and app observations (notes: slice finished, hand setup change, calibration handover). The doc names "state changes your application observes" as a use case and distinguishes a user message (from the end user) from a system message (from the operator) |
| End user | `user` | The person's words plus what travels with them: workspace block, plate picture, file report. Kept in the record as sent (closes R4) |
| Tool results | `tool_result` / `function_call_output` | Their own channel, never promoted; the doc forbids relaying third-party content through system messages |

**Lifetimes.** Skills and the reminder clear at the next user message on Anthropic (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`, beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`). OpenAI has no clear, so they stay visible and should be kept short. Notes the model replied to stay visible on both providers. Thinking/reasoning is stored per chat and replayed.

**Behaviour changes, so evals are required.** Kenneth confirmed this changes what the model reads. Per his 2026-10-19 rule (last confirmed results are the baseline), every behaviour-changing step runs live prompt evals against a baseline. Baselines needed before any such step: OpenAI journeys (none exist) and the prompt-case set (check the last confirmed model and date). Request-body logging in the harness comes before all of it.

**Risks recorded, not resolved:**

- `clear_at` is a beta feature.
- Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result, so a note landing there needs a placement rule.
- OpenAI accumulates visible skill text (1.3–8.5 KB each); whether that changes answers is an eval question.
- Unverified whether the top-level `system` field and in-array system messages may coexist in one request (the doc implies yes).
- Unverified how the JusPrin Cloud gateway passes in-array system messages through in its Anthropic wire format. Production goes through the gateway, so check before R7.
- Corrections the side session made to its own earlier claims, so the tracker does not carry them: Anthropic does accept system messages inside `messages` on 5.x models; OpenAI's `instructions` parameter inserts a system/developer message rather than sitting above both.

# Provider prompt-caching rules, and where JusPrin's codecs fall short

Working doc, 2026-10-28, for the chat-history cache plan (task M2). Untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.

Both providers cache only an unchanged opening of the request, so an append-only history is necessary on both. It is not enough on either. Anthropic also needs cache markers in the right places, the same thinking and effort settings, and a request within 5 minutes (or 1 hour at extra cost). OpenAI needs requests routed to the same machine, which for the model JusPrin uses means a `prompt_cache_key`; JusPrin sends none. Every rule below was read from the provider's docs on 2026-10-28. "Inference" marks what I concluded rather than read.

Sources:
- [A1] Anthropic prompt caching: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
- [A2] Anthropic thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking
- [A3] Anthropic preserved thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking
- [O1] OpenAI prompt caching: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching
- [O2] OpenAI reasoning: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning

## 1. Anthropic (Messages API, `AnthropicCodec.cpp`)

| Topic | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Identical prefix | "Cache hits require 100 percent identical prompt segments, including all text and images up to and including the block marked with cache control." | A1 |
| Prefix order | The prefix is `tools`, then `system`, then `messages`, in that order. A change at one level invalidates that level and every later one. | A1 |
| Markers | Caching happens only at `cache_control` breakpoints, or at the automatic one a top-level `cache_control` adds. "Marking a block with `cache_control` writes exactly one cache entry"; no entry is written for any earlier position. At most 4 breakpoints per request, and the automatic one takes one of the 4. | A1 |
| Where markers may go | Tool definitions, `system` blocks, text blocks in user and assistant turns, images and documents in user turns, `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks. Not on thinking blocks, citations or empty text blocks. | A1 |
| Moving a marker | Moving a breakpoint is the documented pattern for a growing chat ("the fourth breakpoint moved to that new final message"). `cache_control` markers sit outside the thinking prefix check: adding, moving or removing them is not an edit. | A1, A3 |
| Lookback | A read looks for an earlier write at the breakpoint, then walks back one block at a time, "at most 20 positions for each breakpoint". A run of consecutive `tool_use` blocks counts as one position, and so does a run of `tool_result` blocks. | A1 |
| Timing | An entry can be read only after the response that wrote it has started. | A1 |
| Minimum length | 512 tokens for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5/5.1 and Mythos 5/5.1. 1,024 tokens for Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 4.x. 2,048 for Opus 4.7. 4,096 for Opus 4.5 and 4.6. A shorter prompt is processed uncached, with no error. | A1 |
| TTL | 5 minutes by default, refreshed free on every read. A 1-hour TTL is available with `"ttl": "1h"`. A longer TTL must come before a shorter one in the request. The lifetime runs from the start of the request. | A1 |
| Price (multiples of the input price) | Writes: 1.25x for 5 minutes, 2x for 1 hour. Reads: 0.1x by default, 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5. | A1 |
| What else invalidates | Tool definitions invalidate everything. `tool_choice` invalidates messages. Adding or removing an image anywhere invalidates messages. A thinking or `output_config.effort` change always invalidates messages, and on some models tools and system too. Per-message effort (a `role: "system"` message, beta) leaves the prefix intact. | A1, A2 |
| Thinking in history | Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5, Fable and Mythos keep every earlier turn's thinking in context, and the cache stays valid when a new user message is added. Earlier models strip earlier turns' thinking, so messages after it leave the cache. A thinking block the current model cannot read (another model's) is dropped, and the cached prefix changes from that block on. | A1, A2 |
| Edits and thinking (correctness, not just cost) | A thinking block is valid only while `system`, `tools` and every message before it are unchanged. For accounts created on or after 2026-08-31 the API checks this on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1, and by default rejects an edited prefix with a 400. With `drop_block` it drops the block and "the prompt cache restarts at the edit". The listed edits include: adding a text block to an earlier user turn or removing one you added last time; re-rendering context in the first user message with a changed value; shortening an earlier `tool_result` or re-encoding an earlier image; changing `system` or `tools`; removing thinking from the middle of the history. Appending at the end and changing `effort`, `max_tokens`, `tool_choice` or `cache_control` are not edits. | A3 |
| Mid-conversation system messages | A `role: "system"` message inside `messages` is supported on current models (not Sonnet 5). In a tool loop it goes after the `tool_result` message, never between `tool_use` and `tool_result`. "Once sent, the message is part of the prefix for later thinking: leave it in place on later requests." | A1, A3 |
| Usage | `cache_read_input_tokens` are tokens read; `cache_creation_input_tokens` are tokens written, broken down by TTL in `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` / `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`. `input_tokens` are only the tokens after the last breakpoint. Total input = read + creation + input_tokens. | A1 |

## 2. OpenAI (Responses API, `ResponsesCodec.cpp`)

JusPrin's OpenAI default is `gpt-5.4-mini`, a model from before GPT-5.6, so the "earlier models" rules apply. OpenRouter's caching is not covered here.

| Topic | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Identical prefix | "Cache reuse requires the entire rendered prefix to match." OpenAI caches the full rendered context: instructions, developer messages, tool definitions, and history with text, images and documents. | O1 |
| Markers | Before GPT-5.6: none. Caching is on by default and "Only implicit caching is supported", with breakpoints placed by OpenAI at model-dependent intervals. GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_options.mode` is `implicit` or `explicit`. Explicit mode takes `prompt_cache_breakpoint` on content blocks inside input messages, never on top-level `instructions`. With no breakpoint placed, explicit mode does not cache at all. Up to 4 writes per request. Implicit mode puts a breakpoint at the end of the latest eligible message and looks back over "up to 20 earlier eligible message endings". The docs do not say which mode is the default. | O1 |
| Routing | Requests go to a machine chosen by "a hash of the initial tokens after the hidden OpenAI content, including tool definitions". The cache lives on that machine. "traffic above 15 requests per minute can lead to overflow routing", and an overflowed request misses. Before GPT-5.6, `prompt_cache_key` "separates cache reuse between groups of requests and helps optimize cache routing"; the advice is about 15 requests per minute per key. GPT-5.6+ does not need the key. | O1 |
| Minimum length | 1,024 visible input tokens on GPT-5.6+. For earlier models it "varies by request settings" (tools, images, schemas, effort, verbosity). Earlier models report `cached_tokens` rounded down to a multiple of 128. | O1 |
| Retention | Earlier models, in memory: "around 5 to 10 minutes of inactivity, up to one hour". Extended `24h` retention (`prompt_cache_retention`) is listed for `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-5` and others. `gpt-5.4-mini` is not on that list. Organizations without Zero Data Retention default to `24h`. GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_options.ttl` of `30m` (default) or `12h`. | O1 |
| Price | Earlier models: no write charge, reads at 0.1x. GPT-5.6+: writes at 1.25x (30 minutes) or 2.5x (12 hours). | O1 |
| What else changes the prefix | `model`, `tools` (names, descriptions, schemas, order), `parallel_tool_calls`, `text.format`, `reasoning.effort`, `text.verbosity`, `context_management`. A `configuration_update` input item changes effort without breaking the prefix (GPT-6). | O1, O2 |
| Reasoning in history | Within a tool loop, pass back every reasoning item with its call. Models before GPT-5.6 do not render earlier turns' reasoning into the next sample; GPT-5.6 renders it by default. With `store: false`, reasoning items carry `encrypted_content` by default; `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` is still accepted but no longer required. Neither guide says how reasoning items affect cache hits. | O2 |
| Usage | `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` is billed reads, excluding writes. On GPT-5.6+, `cache_write_tokens` gives writes, split into `ttl_30m_tokens` and `ttl_12h_tokens`. | O1 |

Inference, not stated in the docs: on a pre-5.6 model, the last request of turn N renders that turn's reasoning, and the first request of turn N+1 no longer does (it is now an earlier turn's reasoning). If that is how rendering works, the rendered prefix changes at turn N's first reasoning item even when JusPrin resends the input byte for byte. In that case, on `gpt-5.4-mini` an append-only history can win back only the turns before the last one. This needs a live check of `cached_tokens` (one cheap OpenAI run, needs Kenneth's approval).

## 3. What the codecs do today

`AnthropicCodec.cpp` places three breakpoints, all with the default 5-minute TTL:
1. on the last tool (`tools_json`, line 87);
2. on the single `system` block (`build`, line 272);
3. on the last block of the newest `user` message (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.

It sends `thinking: adaptive` and `output_config.effort` from the chat's model choice, replays each response's own blocks (thinking included) within a turn, keeps fired skills in place for the rest of the turn, and reads `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.

`ResponsesCodec.cpp` sends `store: false`, `parallel_tool_calls: true`, `instructions`, `tools`, `input`, and `reasoning.effort` when set. It sends no `prompt_cache_key`, no `prompt_cache_retention` and no `include`. It replays each response's own items (reasoning included) within a turn. It sends fired skills only as the last items of the request where they fired, and drops them from the next request. It reads `cached_tokens` only.

## 4. Gaps

The first three are what the guard test in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (`[history-prefix]`) catches; the rest it cannot see, because they are about markers, settings, timing or routing, not the bytes of the history.

1. **Earlier turns are rewritten between turns (both codecs).** The host replays them as text: no thinking, no workspace block, no pictures, no skills, results as stored, app notes missing. This breaks the identical-prefix rule [A1, O1]. On Anthropic, once thinking is carried across turns (plan step R7), the same edits become 400 errors for accounts created after 2026-08-31 [A3]. Removing a workspace block from an earlier user turn, re-rendering the file-load reminder in the first message, and cutting a stored result are each named as edits there.
2. **Responses drops a fired skill from the next request** (mid-turn, and on the next turn). That changes the middle of the input [O1]. Anthropic's codec already keeps them, which matches "leave it in place on later requests" [A3].

# Chat history measurement (M1)

No recorded source holds the full request bodies of a live chat. The two Opus 5.5 runs logged only one usage line per request (token counts) and the stored chat record, with every tool result cut to 4,000 characters by the harness. The only full request bodies on disk are 26 scripted ones in `tests/project_prompt/requests.json`. The app built them itself in OpenAI format, but no model was called, and each case is a single request, not a chat.

Working doc, 2026-10-29, for task M1 in `chat-history-cache-plan.md`. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`. The scripts that produced every number are in the side-session notes folder, `…/side-session-notes/local_34d95bfb-fc90-47e6-94ab-adc3d3711d01/m1-scripts/` (`measure_bodies.py`, `measure_opus.py`, `tables.py`). Anything marked **inference** is my reading, not a measurement.

## Summary

In both data sets, none of the size limits on the replayed history ever fired on a recorded request. The largest replayed history in the 26 recorded bodies is 11,881 bytes by the host's own count, against a 64 KiB budget. The largest in the six live Opus chats is at most about 13,000 tokens. That is under 64 KiB at any plausible bytes-per-token ratio. No replayed result in the recorded bodies was over 16 KiB. One live result probably was: the bunny chat's `object_analyze`, an estimated 17–19 KB, so it would have been cut on the bunny's last turn. That is an **inference** from token growth, because the harness cut its stored copy at 4,000 characters.

What does change every request between turns is the material that goes only with the current request:
- the `<workspace>` block on each live tool result (1.0–1.7 KB each, about 60% of in-turn tool-result bytes)
- the `<workspace>` block on the person's message (0.5–0.95 KB)
- fired skill text (1.3–8.5 KB)
- the plate picture
- (**inference**) the model's thinking

At each turn start, the Opus runs dropped at least 3,500–9,000 tokens of what the previous request had sent, and then rewrote everything after the 15,210-token system-and-tools prefix (1,311–12,901 tokens). Those rewrites were 24% of all cache-write tokens in the baseline run. The prototype brought that to 3% and left the first turn after a file load as the only miss.

## Sources

I read this as the skill text sitting after the newest cache breakpoint, which `AnthropicCodec::build` puts on the last user content. So the skill is written to cache one request late. That costs a few thousand tokens per run. I did not confirm the layout from a body.

The handoff (section 3) blames this flip; the usage lines are consistent with that but cannot prove it. It is 215 bytes. |

## What this data cannot show

- **The exact content of any live Opus request.** There are no bodies, so the split of each turn-boundary drop between thinking, workspace blocks, skills and pictures is inference.
- **Real sizes of large live results.** The harness kept 4,000 characters of each result. The bunny's `object_analyze` size, and whether it crossed 16 KiB, is an estimate.
- **Chats longer than three turns.** No recording has more than two earlier turns of history, or more than one model. The 64 KiB budget was sized for "about ten turns". This data neither confirms nor refutes that.
- **The real distribution of tool results.** The 3,113 answers are a catalogue built to cover every read a model might make, and the 26 bodies are scripted single requests.
- **Answer quality.** Nothing here shows whether the cut, the trim or the dropped material ever made a model answer worse, or whether a model calls a tool again after an omission note.
- **OpenAI caching.** The recorded bodies are OpenAI-shaped but were never sent. No usage lines exist for an OpenAI chat on the current code (plan task M4).
- **The tool list changing between turns.** From reading `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp`: `object_import` is offered only when the request has an importable attachment, and on Anthropic the tools come first, so a change there would void the whole cache. The one recorded body with its own tool list (`model-imported-by-tool`) was recorded at a different time from the others, so it cannot show this cleanly. Not measured.
- **The `once` counts.** `requests.json`'s `once` field, how many trailing items go on one request only, was used only to cross-check the skill and picture positions.

I read this as the skill text sitting after the newest cache breakpoint, which `AnthropicCodec::build` puts on the last user content. So the skill is written to cache one request late. That costs a few thousand tokens per run. I did not confirm the layout from a body.

| Skills not replayed | **Yes, every chat.** | 8,522 bytes (2,537 tokens) on turn 0 and 1,331 bytes (441 tokens) on each person-started turn, never seen again later. |
| File-load reminder only when no skill fired | **Yes, every chat.** | Absent on turn 0, where a skill fired, and present from turn 1. It sits at the very front of the history, so it moves the first message. Every turn-1 start missed in the prototype run too (`out/*/harness.log`, `cached_input_tokens=15210`). The handoff (section 3) blames this flip; the usage lines are consistent with that but cannot prove it. It is 215 bytes. |
| App notes excluded | **Yes, but tiny.** | "The slice of Plate 1 finished." starts each app turn (`turn-1.json` messages with role `note`) and is not replayed after. That is about 30 bytes. |

## What this data cannot show

- **The exact content of any live Opus request.** There are no bodies, so the split of each turn-boundary drop between thinking, workspace blocks, skills and pictures is inference.
- **Real sizes of large live results.** The harness kept 4,000 characters of each result. The bunny's `object_analyze` size, and whether it crossed 16 KiB, is an estimate.
- **Chats longer than three turns.** No recording has more than two earlier turns of history, or more than one model. The 64 KiB budget was sized for "about ten turns". This data neither confirms nor refutes that.
- **The real distribution of tool results.** The 3,113 answers are a catalogue built to cover every read a model might make, and the 26 bodies are scripted single requests.
- **Answer quality.** Nothing here shows whether the cut, the trim or the dropped material ever made a model answer worse, or whether a model calls a tool again after an omission note.
- **OpenAI caching.** The recorded bodies are OpenAI-shaped but were never sent. No usage lines exist for an OpenAI chat on the current code (plan task M4).
- **The tool list changing between turns.** From reading `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp`: `object_import` is offered only when the request has an importable attachment, and on Anthropic the tools come first, so a change there would void the whole cache. The one recorded body with its own tool list (`model-imported-by-tool`) was recorded at a different time from the others, so it cannot show this cleanly. Not measured.
- **The `once` counts.** `requests.json`'s `once` field, how many trailing items go on one request only, was used only to cross-check the skill and picture positions.

# Chat history measurement (M1)

No recorded source holds the full request bodies of a live chat. The two Opus 5.5 runs logged only one usage line per request (token counts) and the stored chat record, with every tool result cut to 4,000 characters by the harness. The only full request bodies on disk are 26 scripted ones in `tests/project_prompt/requests.json`. The app built them itself in OpenAI format, but no model was called, and each case is a single request, not a chat.

Working doc, 2026-10-29, for task M1 in `chat-history-cache-plan.md`. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`. The scripts that produced every number are in the side-session notes folder, `…/side-session-notes/local_34d95bfb-fc90-47e6-94ab-adc3d3711d01/m1-scripts/` (`measure_bodies.py`, `measure_opus.py`, `tables.py`). Anything marked **inference** is my reading, not a measurement.

## Summary

In both data sets, none of the size limits on the replayed history ever fired on a recorded request. The largest replayed history in the 26 recorded bodies is 11,881 bytes by the host's own count, against a 64 KiB budget. The largest in the six live Opus chats is at most about 13,000 tokens. That is under 64 KiB at any plausible bytes-per-token ratio. No replayed result in the recorded bodies was over 16 KiB. One live result probably was: the bunny chat's `object_analyze`, an estimated 17–19 KB, so it would have been cut on the bunny's last turn. That is an **inference** from token growth, because the harness cut its stored copy at 4,000 characters.

What does change every request between turns is the material that goes only with the current request:
- the `<workspace>` block on each live tool result (1.0–1.7 KB each, about 60% of in-turn tool-result bytes)
- the `<workspace>` block on the person's message (0.5–0.95 KB)
- fired skill text (1.3–8.5 KB)
- the plate picture
- (**inference**) the model's thinking

At each turn start, the Opus runs dropped at least 3,500–9,000 tokens of what the previous request had sent, and then rewrote everything after the 15,210-token system-and-tools prefix (1,311–12,901 tokens). Those rewrites were 24% of all cache-write tokens in the baseline run. The prototype brought that to 3% and left the first turn after a file load as the only miss.

The harness checked the system prompt against `projectInstructions.fixture.txt` and the tools against `project_tools.json`, then left both out of the file. 3,113 recorded tool results ("answers") sit beside the bodies. | Yes, minus system prompt and tools, which are measured from those two files |

The turn-start rows show the cost of retelling. It is concentrated on the turn the app starts after a slice, because that turn follows the longest turn.

**A second, smaller leak (inference).** Two patterns repeat across all six chats:
- Every request that carries a fired skill has that many tokens billed uncached: 2,537 on each turn-0 request, 441 on the request after `setup_record` (9,375 per run).
- On the next request the cache read stops that many tokens short of the previous input.

I read this as the skill text sitting after the newest cache breakpoint, which `AnthropicCodec::build` puts on the last user content. So the skill is written to cache one request late. That costs a few thousand tokens per run. I did not confirm the layout from a body.

## Which size optimizations changed a real request in this data

| Optimization | Did it change a recorded request? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 16 KiB cut of a replayed result | **Not in the recorded bodies; probably once in the Opus runs.** | 0 of the 41 results in the 26 bodies exceeds 16 KiB; the largest is 10,454. The 26 answers over 16 KiB are the recorder's own printer-scope `settings_get`, which no body contains. Opus: the bunny's `object_analyze` (an estimated 17–19 KB, **inference**) would have been cut on the baseline bunny's app-started turn. The prototype carried that turn as sent instead (`out/bunny/harness.log` shows no turn-start miss). |
| 64 KiB rolling trim | **Never.** | Largest replayed history: 11,881 bytes in the bodies, about 27 KB by reconstruction in the Opus records, under 13,000 tokens in the usage lines. |
| Pictures excluded from later turns | **Yes, every chat.** | The plate picture on every turn-0 request (25–202 KB base64 in the bodies, about 1,050 Anthropic tokens by estimate) is absent from turn 1. So are the bunny's `view_render` pictures at its later turn start. Part of the ≥3,500-token drop at each file-load boundary (**inference** on the split). |
| Workspace snapshots excluded from replayed turns | **Yes, every turn.** | Within a turn every live result carries a 1.0–1.7 KB workspace block (`after-apply`: 11,692 of 20,865 bytes), and the person's message carries 0.5–0.95 KB. None of the replayed history in the bodies carries one. In the Opus runs they are part of the 4,100–9,000 tokens dropped at each later boundary (**inference** on the split). |
| Skills not replayed | **Yes, every chat.** | 8,522 bytes (2,537 tokens) on turn 0 and 1,331 bytes (441 tokens) on each person-started turn, never seen again later. |
| File-load reminder only when no skill fired | **Yes, every chat.** | Absent on turn 0, where a skill fired, and present from turn 1. It sits at the very front of the history, so it moves the first message. Every turn-1 start missed in the prototype run too (`out/*/harness.log`, `cached_input_tokens=15210`). The handoff (section 3) blames this flip; the usage lines are consistent with that but cannot prove it. It is 215 bytes. |
| App notes excluded | **Yes, but tiny.** | "The slice of Plate 1 finished." starts each app turn (`turn-1.json` messages with role `note`) and is not replayed after. That is about 30 bytes. |

## What this data cannot show

- **The exact content of any live Opus request.** There are no bodies, so the split of each turn-boundary drop between thinking, workspace blocks, skills and pictures is inference.
- **Real sizes of large live results.** The harness kept 4,000 characters of each result. The bunny's `object_analyze` size, and whether it crossed 16 KiB, is an estimate.
- **Chats longer than three turns.** No recording has more than two earlier turns of history, or more than one model. The 64 KiB budget was sized for "about ten turns". This data neither confirms nor refutes that.
- **The real distribution of tool results.** The 3,113 answers are a catalogue built to cover every read a model might make, and the 26 bodies are scripted single requests.
- **Answer quality.** Nothing here shows whether the cut, the trim or the dropped material ever made a model answer worse, or whether a model calls a tool again after an omission note.
- **OpenAI caching.** The recorded bodies are OpenAI-shaped but were never sent. No usage lines exist for an OpenAI chat on the current code (plan task M4).
- **The tool list changing between turns.** From reading `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp`: `object_import` is offered only when the request has an importable attachment, and on Anthropic the tools come first, so a change there would void the whole cache. The one recorded body with its own tool list (`model-imported-by-tool`) was recorded at a different time from the others, so it cannot show this cleanly. Not measured.
- **The `once` counts.** `requests.json`'s `once` field, how many trailing items go on one request only, was used only to cross-check the skill and picture positions.

## Roles and lifetimes in the request (approved 2026-10-29)

Decided by Kenneth in the side session "Chat history cache handoff" (`local_97f342dd-4367-4bc5-830d-1c6d6d91db47`), relayed to this doc; his words: "ok. go with your proposal." The provider-doc citations below are that session's, not re-verified here.

**Append-only record, separate from visibility.** Each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent to the model. A request renders that record plus the new items. No item is rewritten, dropped or re-derived; what the model should still see is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. Source cited: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages doc (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`): a cleared message stays in the array but renders nothing, must be re-sent verbatim, and rebuilding or dropping it counts as an edit to an earlier message that fails the thinking check and breaks the cache.

**Three roles, assigned by who speaks, never by lifetime:**

| Role | Wire | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| Operator, standing | Anthropic top-level `system`; Responses `instructions` | Standing prompt and tools, written once per chat, never changed |
| Operator, in conversation | Anthropic in-array `role:"system"` (Opus 5.5 and 5.x, not Sonnet 5); OpenAI `developer` item | Situational instructions (skills; the file-load reminder if it survives D4) and app observations (notes: slice finished, hand setup change, calibration handover). The doc names "state changes your application observes" as a use case and distinguishes a user message (from the end user) from a system message (from the operator) |
| End user | `user` | The person's words plus what travels with them: workspace block, plate picture, file report. Kept in the record as sent (closes R4) |
| Tool results | `tool_result` / `function_call_output` | Their own channel, never promoted; the doc forbids relaying third-party content through system messages |

**Lifetimes.** Skills and the reminder clear at the next user message on Anthropic (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`, beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`). OpenAI has no clear, so they stay visible and should be kept short. Notes the model replied to stay visible on both providers. Thinking/reasoning is stored per chat and replayed.

**Behaviour changes, so evals are required.** Kenneth confirmed this changes what the model reads. Per his 2026-10-19 rule (last confirmed results are the baseline), every behaviour-changing step runs live prompt evals against a baseline. Baselines needed before any such step: OpenAI journeys (none exist) and the prompt-case set (check the last confirmed model and date). Request-body logging in the harness comes before all of it.

**Risks recorded, not resolved:**

- `clear_at` is a beta feature.
- Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result, so a note landing there needs a placement rule.
- OpenAI accumulates visible skill text (1.3–8.5 KB each); whether that changes answers is an eval question.
- Unverified whether the top-level `system` field and in-array system messages may coexist in one request (the doc implies yes).
- Unverified how the JusPrin Cloud gateway passes in-array system messages through in its Anthropic wire format. Production goes through the gateway, so check before R7.
- Corrections the side session made to its own earlier claims, so the tracker does not carry them: Anthropic does accept system messages inside `messages` on 5.x models; OpenAI's `instructions` parameter inserts a system/developer message rather than sitting above both.

# Provider prompt-caching rules, and where JusPrin's codecs fall short

Working doc, 2026-10-28, for the chat-history cache plan (task M2). Untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.

Both providers cache only an unchanged opening of the request, so an append-only history is necessary on both. It is not enough on either. Anthropic also needs cache markers in the right places, the same thinking and effort settings, and a request within 5 minutes (or 1 hour at extra cost). OpenAI needs requests routed to the same machine, which for the model JusPrin uses means a `prompt_cache_key`; JusPrin sends none. Every rule below was read from the provider's docs on 2026-10-28. "Inference" marks what I concluded rather than read.

Sources:
- [A1] Anthropic prompt caching: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
- [A2] Anthropic thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking
- [A3] Anthropic preserved thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking
- [O1] OpenAI prompt caching: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching
- [O2] OpenAI reasoning: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning

## 1. Anthropic (Messages API, `AnthropicCodec.cpp`)

| Topic | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Identical prefix | "Cache hits require 100 percent identical prompt segments, including all text and images up to and including the block marked with cache control." | A1 |
| Prefix order | The prefix is `tools`, then `system`, then `messages`, in that order. A change at one level invalidates that level and every later one. | A1 |
| Markers | Caching happens only at `cache_control` breakpoints, or at the automatic one a top-level `cache_control` adds. "Marking a block with `cache_control` writes exactly one cache entry"; no entry is written for any earlier position. At most 4 breakpoints per request, and the automatic one takes one of the 4. | A1 |
| Where markers may go | Tool definitions, `system` blocks, text blocks in user and assistant turns, images and documents in user turns, `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks. Not on thinking blocks, citations or empty text blocks. | A1 |
| Moving a marker | Moving a breakpoint is the documented pattern for a growing chat ("the fourth breakpoint moved to that new final message"). `cache_control` markers sit outside the thinking prefix check: adding, moving or removing them is not an edit. | A1, A3 |
| Lookback | A read looks for an earlier write at the breakpoint, then walks back one block at a time, "at most 20 positions for each breakpoint". A run of consecutive `tool_use` blocks counts as one position, and so does a run of `tool_result` blocks. | A1 |
| Timing | An entry can be read only after the response that wrote it has started. | A1 |
| Minimum length | 512 tokens for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5/5.1 and Mythos 5/5.1. 1,024 tokens for Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 4.x. 2,048 for Opus 4.7. 4,096 for Opus 4.5 and 4.6. A shorter prompt is processed uncached, with no error. | A1 |
| TTL | 5 minutes by default, refreshed free on every read. A 1-hour TTL is available with `"ttl": "1h"`. A longer TTL must come before a shorter one in the request. The lifetime runs from the start of the request. | A1 |
| Price (multiples of the input price) | Writes: 1.25x for 5 minutes, 2x for 1 hour. Reads: 0.1x by default, 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5. | A1 |
| What else invalidates | Tool definitions invalidate everything. `tool_choice` invalidates messages. Adding or removing an image anywhere invalidates messages. A thinking or `output_config.effort` change always invalidates messages, and on some models tools and system too. Per-message effort (a `role: "system"` message, beta) leaves the prefix intact. | A1, A2 |
| Thinking in history | Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5, Fable and Mythos keep every earlier turn's thinking in context, and the cache stays valid when a new user message is added. Earlier models strip earlier turns' thinking, so messages after it leave the cache. A thinking block the current model cannot read (another model's) is dropped, and the cached prefix changes from that block on. | A1, A2 |
| Edits and thinking (correctness, not just cost) | A thinking block is valid only while `system`, `tools` and every message before it are unchanged. For accounts created on or after 2026-08-31 the API checks this on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1, and by default rejects an edited prefix with a 400. With `drop_block` it drops the block and "the prompt cache restarts at the edit". The listed edits include: adding a text block to an earlier user turn or removing one you added last time; re-rendering context in the first user message with a changed value; shortening an earlier `tool_result` or re-encoding an earlier image; changing `system` or `tools`; removing thinking from the middle of the history. Appending at the end and changing `effort`, `max_tokens`, `tool_choice` or `cache_control` are not edits. | A3 |
| Mid-conversation system messages | A `role: "system"` message inside `messages` is supported on current models (not Sonnet 5). In a tool loop it goes after the `tool_result` message, never between `tool_use` and `tool_result`. "Once sent, the message is part of the prefix for later thinking: leave it in place on later requests." | A1, A3 |
| Usage | `cache_read_input_tokens` are tokens read; `cache_creation_input_tokens` are tokens written, broken down by TTL in `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` / `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`. `input_tokens` are only the tokens after the last breakpoint. Total input = read + creation + input_tokens. | A1 |

## 2. OpenAI (Responses API, `ResponsesCodec.cpp`)

JusPrin's OpenAI default is `gpt-5.4-mini`, a model from before GPT-5.6, so the "earlier models" rules apply. OpenRouter's caching is not covered here.

| Topic | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Identical prefix | "Cache reuse requires the entire rendered prefix to match." OpenAI caches the full rendered context: instructions, developer messages, tool definitions, and history with text, images and documents. | O1 |
| Markers | Before GPT-5.6: none. Caching is on by default and "Only implicit caching is supported", with breakpoints placed by OpenAI at model-dependent intervals. GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_options.mode` is `implicit` or `explicit`. Explicit mode takes `prompt_cache_breakpoint` on content blocks inside input messages, never on top-level `instructions`. With no breakpoint placed, explicit mode does not cache at all. Up to 4 writes per request. Implicit mode puts a breakpoint at the end of the latest eligible message and looks back over "up to 20 earlier eligible message endings". The docs do not say which mode is the default. | O1 |
| Routing | Requests go to a machine chosen by "a hash of the initial tokens after the hidden OpenAI content, including tool definitions". The cache lives on that machine. "traffic above 15 requests per minute can lead to overflow routing", and an overflowed request misses. Before GPT-5.6, `prompt_cache_key` "separates cache reuse between groups of requests and helps optimize cache routing"; the advice is about 15 requests per minute per key. GPT-5.6+ does not need the key. | O1 |
| Minimum length | 1,024 visible input tokens on GPT-5.6+. For earlier models it "varies by request settings" (tools, images, schemas, effort, verbosity). Earlier models report `cached_tokens` rounded down to a multiple of 128. | O1 |
| Retention | Earlier models, in memory: "around 5 to 10 minutes of inactivity, up to one hour". Extended `24h` retention (`prompt_cache_retention`) is listed for `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-5` and others. `gpt-5.4-mini` is not on that list. Organizations without Zero Data Retention default to `24h`. GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_options.ttl` of `30m` (default) or `12h`. | O1 |
| Price | Earlier models: no write charge, reads at 0.1x. GPT-5.6+: writes at 1.25x (30 minutes) or 2.5x (12 hours). | O1 |
| What else changes the prefix | `model`, `tools` (names, descriptions, schemas, order), `parallel_tool_calls`, `text.format`, `reasoning.effort`, `text.verbosity`, `context_management`. A `configuration_update` input item changes effort without breaking the prefix (GPT-6). | O1, O2 |
| Reasoning in history | Within a tool loop, pass back every reasoning item with its call. Models before GPT-5.6 do not render earlier turns' reasoning into the next sample; GPT-5.6 renders it by default. With `store: false`, reasoning items carry `encrypted_content` by default; `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` is still accepted but no longer required. Neither guide says how reasoning items affect cache hits. | O2 |
| Usage | `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` is billed reads, excluding writes. On GPT-5.6+, `cache_write_tokens` gives writes, split into `ttl_30m_tokens` and `ttl_12h_tokens`. | O1 |

Inference, not stated in the docs: on a pre-5.6 model, the last request of turn N renders that turn's reasoning, and the first request of turn N+1 no longer does (it is now an earlier turn's reasoning). If that is how rendering works, the rendered prefix changes at turn N's first reasoning item even when JusPrin resends the input byte for byte. In that case, on `gpt-5.4-mini` an append-only history can win back only the turns before the last one. This needs a live check of `cached_tokens` (one cheap OpenAI run, needs Kenneth's approval).

## 3. What the codecs do today

`AnthropicCodec.cpp` places three breakpoints, all with the default 5-minute TTL:
1. on the last tool (`tools_json`, line 87);
2. on the single `system` block (`build`, line 272);
3. on the last block of the newest `user` message (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.

It sends `thinking: adaptive` and `output_config.effort` from the chat's model choice, replays each response's own blocks (thinking included) within a turn, keeps fired skills in place for the rest of the turn, and reads `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.

`ResponsesCodec.cpp` sends `store: false`, `parallel_tool_calls: true`, `instructions`, `tools`, `input`, and `reasoning.effort` when set. It sends no `prompt_cache_key`, no `prompt_cache_retention` and no `include`. It replays each response's own items (reasoning included) within a turn. It sends fired skills only as the last items of the request where they fired, and drops them from the next request. It reads `cached_tokens` only.

## 4. Gaps

The first three are what the guard test in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (`[history-prefix]`) catches; the rest it cannot see, because they are about markers, settings, timing or routing, not the bytes of the history.

1. **Earlier turns are rewritten between turns (both codecs).** The host replays them as text: no thinking, no workspace block, no pictures, no skills, results as stored, app notes missing. This breaks the identical-prefix rule [A1, O1]. On Anthropic, once thinking is carried across turns (plan step R7), the same edits become 400 errors for accounts created after 2026-08-31 [A3]. Removing a workspace block from an earlier user turn, re-rendering the file-load reminder in the first message, and cutting a stored result are each named as edits there.
2. **Responses drops a fired skill from the next request** (mid-turn, and on the next turn). That changes the middle of the input [O1]. Anthropic's codec already keeps them, which matches "leave it in place on later requests" [A3].

1	# Provider prompt-caching rules, and where JusPrin's codecs fall short
2	
3	Working doc, 2026-10-28, for the chat-history cache plan (task M2). Untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
4	
5	Both providers cache only an unchanged opening of the request, so an append-only history is necessary on both. It is not enough on either. Anthropic also needs cache markers in the right places, the same thinking and effort settings, and a request within 5 minutes (or 1 hour at extra cost). OpenAI needs requests routed to the same machine, which for the model JusPrin uses means a `prompt_cache_key`; JusPrin sends none. Every rule below was read from the provider's docs on 2026-10-28. "Inference" marks what I concluded rather than read.
6	
7	Sources:
8	- [A1] Anthropic prompt caching: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
9	- [A2] Anthropic thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking
10	- [A3] Anthropic preserved thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking
11	- [O1] OpenAI prompt caching: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching
12	- [O2] OpenAI reasoning: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning
13	
14	## 1. Anthropic (Messages API, `AnthropicCodec.cpp`)
15	
16	| Topic | Rule | Source |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| Identical prefix | "Cache hits require 100 percent identical prompt segments, including all text and images up to and including the block marked with cache control." | A1 |
19	| Prefix order | The prefix is `tools`, then `system`, then `messages`, in that order. A change at one level invalidates that level and every later one. | A1 |
20	| Markers | Caching happens only at `cache_control` breakpoints, or at the automatic one a top-level `cache_control` adds. "Marking a block with `cache_control` writes exactly one cache entry"; no entry is written for any earlier position. At most 4 breakpoints per request, and the automatic one takes one of the 4. | A1 |
21	| Where markers may go | Tool definitions, `system` blocks, text blocks in user and assistant turns, images and documents in user turns, `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks. Not on thinking blocks, citations or empty text blocks. | A1 |
22	| Moving a marker | Moving a breakpoint is the documented pattern for a growing chat ("the fourth breakpoint moved to that new final message"). `cache_control` markers sit outside the thinking prefix check: adding, moving or removing them is not an edit. | A1, A3 |
23	| Lookback | A read looks for an earlier write at the breakpoint, then walks back one block at a time, "at most 20 positions for each breakpoint". A run of consecutive `tool_use` blocks counts as one position, and so does a run of `tool_result` blocks. | A1 |
24	| Timing | An entry can be read only after the response that wrote it has started. | A1 |
25	| Minimum length | 512 tokens for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5/5.1 and Mythos 5/5.1. 1,024 tokens for Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 4.x. 2,048 for Opus 4.7. 4,096 for Opus 4.5 and 4.6. A shorter prompt is processed uncached, with no error. | A1 |
26	| TTL | 5 minutes by default, refreshed free on every read. A 1-hour TTL is available with `"ttl": "1h"`. A longer TTL must come before a shorter one in the request. The lifetime runs from the start of the request. | A1 |
27	| Price (multiples of the input price) | Writes: 1.25x for 5 minutes, 2x for 1 hour. Reads: 0.1x by default, 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5. | A1 |
28	| What else invalidates | Tool definitions invalidate everything. `tool_choice` invalidates messages. Adding or removing an image anywhere invalidates messages. A thinking or `output_config.effort` change always invalidates messages, and on some models tools and system too. Per-message effort (a `role: "system"` message, beta) leaves the prefix intact. | A1, A2 |
29	| Thinking in history | Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5, Fable and Mythos keep every earlier turn's thinking in context, and the cache stays valid when a new user message is added. Earlier models strip earlier turns' thinking, so messages after it leave the cache. A thinking block the current model cannot read (another model's) is dropped, and the cached prefix changes from that block on. | A1, A2 |
30	| Edits and thinking (correctness, not just cost) | A thinking block is valid only while `system`, `tools` and every message before it are unchanged. For accounts created on or after 2026-08-31 the API checks this on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1, and by default rejects an edited prefix with a 400. With `drop_block` it drops the block and "the prompt cache restarts at the edit". The listed edits include: adding a text block to an earlier user turn or removing one you added last time; re-rendering context in the first user message with a changed value; shortening an earlier `tool_result` or re-encoding an earlier image; changing `system` or `tools`; removing thinking from the middle of the history. Appending at the end and changing `effort`, `max_tokens`, `tool_choice` or `cache_control` are not edits. | A3 |
31	| Mid-conversation system messages | A `role: "system"` message inside `messages` is supported on current models (not Sonnet 5). In a tool loop it goes after the `tool_result` message, never between `tool_use` and `tool_result`. "Once sent, the message is part of the prefix for later thinking: leave it in place on later requests." | A1, A3 |
32	| Usage | `cache_read_input_tokens` are tokens read; `cache_creation_input_tokens` are tokens written, broken down by TTL in `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` / `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`. `input_tokens` are only the tokens after the last breakpoint. Total input = read + creation + input_tokens. | A1 |
33	
34	## 2. OpenAI (Responses API, `ResponsesCodec.cpp`)
35	
36	JusPrin's OpenAI default is `gpt-5.4-mini`, a model from before GPT-5.6, so the "earlier models" rules apply. OpenRouter's caching is not covered here.
37	
38	| Topic | Rule | Source |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| Identical prefix | "Cache reuse requires the entire rendered prefix to match." OpenAI caches the full rendered context: instructions, developer messages, tool definitions, and history with text, images and documents. | O1 |
41	| Markers | Before GPT-5.6: none. Caching is on by default and "Only implicit caching is supported", with breakpoints placed by OpenAI at model-dependent intervals. GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_options.mode` is `implicit` or `explicit`. Explicit mode takes `prompt_cache_breakpoint` on content blocks inside input messages, never on top-level `instructions`. With no breakpoint placed, explicit mode does not cache at all. Up to 4 writes per request. Implicit mode puts a breakpoint at the end of the latest eligible message and looks back over "up to 20 earlier eligible message endings". The docs do not say which mode is the default. | O1 |
42	| Routing | Requests go to a machine chosen by "a hash of the initial tokens after the hidden OpenAI content, including tool definitions". The cache lives on that machine. "traffic above 15 requests per minute can lead to overflow routing", and an overflowed request misses. Before GPT-5.6, `prompt_cache_key` "separates cache reuse between groups of requests and helps optimize cache routing"; the advice is about 15 requests per minute per key. GPT-5.6+ does not need the key. | O1 |
43	| Minimum length | 1,024 visible input tokens on GPT-5.6+. For earlier models it "varies by request settings" (tools, images, schemas, effort, verbosity). Earlier models report `cached_tokens` rounded down to a multiple of 128. | O1 |
44	| Retention | Earlier models, in memory: "around 5 to 10 minutes of inactivity, up to one hour". Extended `24h` retention (`prompt_cache_retention`) is listed for `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-5` and others. `gpt-5.4-mini` is not on that list. Organizations without Zero Data Retention default to `24h`. GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_options.ttl` of `30m` (default) or `12h`. | O1 |
45	| Price | Earlier models: no write charge, reads at 0.1x. GPT-5.6+: writes at 1.25x (30 minutes) or 2.5x (12 hours). | O1 |
46	| What else changes the prefix | `model`, `tools` (names, descriptions, schemas, order), `parallel_tool_calls`, `text.format`, `reasoning.effort`, `text.verbosity`, `context_management`. A `configuration_update` input item changes effort without breaking the prefix (GPT-6). | O1, O2 |
47	| Reasoning in history | Within a tool loop, pass back every reasoning item with its call. Models before GPT-5.6 do not render earlier turns' reasoning into the next sample; GPT-5.6 renders it by default. With `store: false`, reasoning items carry `encrypted_content` by default; `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` is still accepted but no longer required. Neither guide says how reasoning items affect cache hits. | O2 |
48	| Usage | `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` is billed reads, excluding writes. On GPT-5.6+, `cache_write_tokens` gives writes, split into `ttl_30m_tokens` and `ttl_12h_tokens`. | O1 |
49	
50	Inference, not stated in the docs: on a pre-5.6 model, the last request of turn N renders that turn's reasoning, and the first request of turn N+1 no longer does (it is now an earlier turn's reasoning). If that is how rendering works, the rendered prefix changes at turn N's first reasoning item even when JusPrin resends the input byte for byte. In that case, on `gpt-5.4-mini` an append-only history can win back only the turns before the last one. This needs a live check of `cached_tokens` (one cheap OpenAI run, needs Kenneth's approval).
51	
52	## 3. What the codecs do today
53	
54	`AnthropicCodec.cpp` places three breakpoints, all with the default 5-minute TTL:
55	1. on the last tool (`tools_json`, line 87);
56	2. on the single `system` block (`build`, line 272);
57	3. on the last block of the newest `user` message (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.
58	
59	It sends `thinking: adaptive` and `output_config.effort` from the chat's model choice, replays each response's own blocks (thinking included) within a turn, keeps fired skills in place for the rest of the turn, and reads `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.
60	
61	`ResponsesCodec.cpp` sends `store: false`, `parallel_tool_calls: true`, `instructions`, `tools`, `input`, and `reasoning.effort` when set. It sends no `prompt_cache_key`, no `prompt_cache_retention` and no `include`. It replays each response's own items (reasoning included) within a turn. It sends fired skills only as the last items of the request where they fired, and drops them from the next request. It reads `cached_tokens` only.
62	
63	## 4. Gaps
64	
65	The first three are what the guard test in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (`[history-prefix]`) catches; the rest it cannot see, because they are about markers, settings, timing or routing, not the bytes of the history.
66	
67	1. **Earlier turns are rewritten between turns (both codecs).** The host replays them as text: no thinking, no workspace block, no pictures, no skills, results as stored, app notes missing. This breaks the identical-prefix rule [A1, O1]. On Anthropic, once thinking is carried across turns (plan step R7), the same edits become 400 errors for accounts created after 2026-08-31 [A3]. Removing a workspace block from an earlier user turn, re-rendering the file-load reminder in the first message, and cutting a stored result are each named as edits there.
68	2. **Responses drops a fired skill from the next request** (mid-turn, and on the next turn). That changes the middle of the input [O1]. Anthropic's codec already keeps them, which matches "leave it in place on later requests" [A3].
69	3. **The file-load reminder at the start of the history appears and disappears** (handoff 4.6). That is a changed first message, the worst place for an edit [A1, A3, O1].
70	4. **No `prompt_cache_key` on Responses.** Every JusPrin user sends the same instructions and tools, so before GPT-5.6 all of them hash to the same machines. Above about 15 requests per minute across all users, requests overflow to other machines and miss [O1]. A per-chat key (for example the project and chat id) keeps each chat on one machine. GPT-5.6+ does not need it.
71	5. **5-minute TTL on Anthropic, in-memory retention on `gpt-5.4-mini`.** A pause longer than 5 minutes (the vase journey had a 6-minute one) loses the whole Anthropic cache, and the next request writes it all again at 1.25x [A1]. Anthropic offers a 1-hour TTL at 2x per write. On OpenAI, `gpt-5.4-mini` is not listed for 24-hour retention, so its entries last 5 to 10 idle minutes [O1]. Whether 1 hour pays depends on how often people pause: it is a measurement question, not a fix.
72	6. **A mid-chat thinking or effort change restarts the cache on both providers** [A1, A2, O1]. The per-chat thinking picker (`1ca65bb087`) allows this. Anthropic's per-message effort (beta) and OpenAI's `configuration_update` (GPT-6) avoid it; neither is used. Model switches start a new cache on any design.
73	7. **Cache writes are not reported by TTL.** The Anthropic codec ignores `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m/1h_input_tokens`. That only matters once a 1-hour TTL is used. The Responses codec ignores `cache_write_tokens`, which only GPT-5.6+ reports and charges for.
74	8. **Lookback distance (low risk).** The moving Anthropic breakpoint is about 3 to 6 positions past the previous write in a normal turn: the response's thinking, text and calls, then the results. The window is 20 positions, and runs of `tool_use` or `tool_result` blocks count as one [A1]. A single response that interleaves more than about 18 thinking and call blocks would miss. Nothing seen so far comes close. A second moving breakpoint would cover it.
75	9. **OpenAI explicit mode (future).** If JusPrin moves to GPT-5.6+ and explicit mode turns out to be the default, a request without `prompt_cache_breakpoint` is not cached at all [O1]. The Responses codec places none. Check the default before switching models.
76	
77	Not a gap: the Anthropic tool and system breakpoints are at the end of fixed content, as recommended [A1]. Prompts are far above the minimum length (about 15,000 tokens of tools and system). The moving breakpoint follows the documented pattern. The Responses codec already gets `encrypted_content` with `store: false` by default [O2].
78

| Usage | `cache_read_input_tokens` are tokens read; `cache_creation_input_tokens` are tokens written, broken down by TTL in `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` / `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`. `input_tokens` are only the tokens after the last breakpoint. Total input = read + creation + input_tokens. | A1 |

## 2. OpenAI (Responses API, `ResponsesCodec.cpp`)

JusPrin's OpenAI default is `gpt-5.4-mini`, a model from before GPT-5.6, so the "earlier models" rules apply. OpenRouter's caching is not covered here.

| Topic | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Identical prefix | "Cache reuse requires the entire rendered prefix to match." OpenAI caches the full rendered context: instructions, developer messages, tool definitions, and history with text, images and documents. | O1 |
| Markers | Before GPT-5.6: none. Caching is on by default and "Only implicit caching is supported", with breakpoints placed by OpenAI at model-dependent intervals. GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_options.mode` is `implicit` or `explicit`. Explicit mode takes `prompt_cache_breakpoint` on content blocks inside input messages, never on top-level `instructions`. With no breakpoint placed, explicit mode does not cache at all. Up to 4 writes per request. Implicit mode puts a breakpoint at the end of the latest eligible message and looks back over "up to 20 earlier eligible message endings". The docs do not say which mode is the default. | O1 |
| Routing | Requests go to a machine chosen by "a hash of the initial tokens after the hidden OpenAI content, including tool definitions". The cache lives on that machine. "traffic above 15 requests per minute can lead to overflow routing", and an overflowed request misses. Before GPT-5.6, `prompt_cache_key` "separates cache reuse between groups of requests and helps optimize cache routing"; the advice is about 15 requests per minute per key. GPT-5.6+ does not need the key. | O1 |
| Minimum length | 1,024 visible input tokens on GPT-5.6+. For earlier models it "varies by request settings" (tools, images, schemas, effort, verbosity). Earlier models report `cached_tokens` rounded down to a multiple of 128. | O1 |
| Retention | Earlier models, in memory: "around 5 to 10 minutes of inactivity, up to one hour". Extended `24h` retention (`prompt_cache_retention`) is listed for `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-5` and others. `gpt-5.4-mini` is not on that list. Organizations without Zero Data Retention default to `24h`. GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_options.ttl` of `30m` (default) or `12h`. | O1 |
| Price | Earlier models: no write charge, reads at 0.1x. GPT-5.6+: writes at 1.25x (30 minutes) or 2.5x (12 hours). | O1 |
| What else changes the prefix | `model`, `tools` (names, descriptions, schemas, order), `parallel_tool_calls`, `text.format`, `reasoning.effort`, `text.verbosity`, `context_management`. A `configuration_update` input item changes effort without breaking the prefix (GPT-6). | O1, O2 |
| Reasoning in history | Within a tool loop, pass back every reasoning item with its call. Models before GPT-5.6 do not render earlier turns' reasoning into the next sample; GPT-5.6 renders it by default. With `store: false`, reasoning items carry `encrypted_content` by default; `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` is still accepted but no longer required. Neither guide says how reasoning items affect cache hits. | O2 |
| Usage | `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` is billed reads, excluding writes. On GPT-5.6+, `cache_write_tokens` gives writes, split into `ttl_30m_tokens` and `ttl_12h_tokens`. | O1 |

Inference, not stated in the docs: on a pre-5.6 model, the last request of turn N renders that turn's reasoning, and the first request of turn N+1 no longer does (it is now an earlier turn's reasoning). If that is how rendering works, the rendered prefix changes at turn N's first reasoning item even when JusPrin resends the input byte for byte. In that case, on `gpt-5.4-mini` an append-only history can win back only the turns before the last one. This needs a live check of `cached_tokens` (one cheap OpenAI run, needs Kenneth's approval).

## 3. What the codecs do today

`AnthropicCodec.cpp` places three breakpoints, all with the default 5-minute TTL:
1. on the last tool (`tools_json`, line 87);
2. on the single `system` block (`build`, line 272);
3. on the last block of the newest `user` message (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.

It sends `thinking: adaptive` and `output_config.effort` from the chat's model choice, replays each response's own blocks (thinking included) within a turn, keeps fired skills in place for the rest of the turn, and reads `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.

`ResponsesCodec.cpp` sends `store: false`, `parallel_tool_calls: true`, `instructions`, `tools`, `input`, and `reasoning.effort` when set. It sends no `prompt_cache_key`, no `prompt_cache_retention` and no `include`. It replays each response's own items (reasoning included) within a turn. It sends fired skills only as the last items of the request where they fired, and drops them from the next request. It reads `cached_tokens` only.

## 4. Gaps

The first three are what the guard test in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (`[history-prefix]`) catches; the rest it cannot see, because they are about markers, settings, timing or routing, not the bytes of the history.

1. **Earlier turns are rewritten between turns (both codecs).** The host replays them as text: no thinking, no workspace block, no pictures, no skills, results as stored, app notes missing. This breaks the identical-prefix rule [A1, O1]. On Anthropic, once thinking is carried across turns (plan step R7), the same edits become 400 errors for accounts created after 2026-08-31 [A3]. Removing a workspace block from an earlier user turn, re-rendering the file-load reminder in the first message, and cutting a stored result are each named as edits there.
2. **Responses drops a fired skill from the next request** (mid-turn, and on the next turn). That changes the middle of the input [O1]. Anthropic's codec already keeps them, which matches "leave it in place on later requests" [A3].
3. **The file-load reminder at the start of the history appears and disappears** (handoff 4.6). That is a changed first message, the worst place for an edit [A1, A3, O1].
4. **No `prompt_cache_key` on Responses.** Every JusPrin user sends the same instructions and tools, so before GPT-5.6 all of them hash to the same machines. Above about 15 requests per minute across all users, requests overflow to other machines and miss [O1]. A per-chat key (for example the project and chat id) keeps each chat on one machine. GPT-5.6+ does not need it.
5. **5-minute TTL on Anthropic, in-memory retention on `gpt-5.4-mini`.** A pause longer than 5 minutes (the vase journey had a 6-minute one) loses the whole Anthropic cache, and the next request writes it all again at 1.25x [A1]. Anthropic offers a 1-hour TTL at 2x per write. On OpenAI, `gpt-5.4-mini` is not listed for 24-hour retention, so its entries last 5 to 10 idle minutes [O1]. Whether 1 hour pays depends on how often people pause: it is a measurement question, not a fix.
6. **A mid-chat thinking or effort change restarts the cache on both providers** [A1, A2, O1]. The per-chat thinking picker (`1ca65bb087`) allows this. Anthropic's per-message effort (beta) and OpenAI's `configuration_update` (GPT-6) avoid it; neither is used. Model switches start a new cache on any design.
7. **Cache writes are not reported by TTL.** The Anthropic codec ignores `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m/1h_input_tokens`. That only matters once a 1-hour TTL is used. The Responses codec ignores `cache_write_tokens`, which only GPT-5.6+ reports and charges for.
8. **Lookback distance (low risk).** The moving Anthropic breakpoint is about 3 to 6 positions past the previous write in a normal turn: the response's thinking, text and calls, then the results. The window is 20 positions, and runs of `tool_use` or `tool_result` blocks count as one [A1]. A single response that interleaves more than about 18 thinking and call blocks would miss. Nothing seen so far comes close. A second moving breakpoint would cover it.
9. **OpenAI explicit mode (future).** If JusPrin moves to GPT-5.6+ and explicit mode turns out to be the default, a request without `prompt_cache_breakpoint` is not cached at all [O1]. The Responses codec places none. Check the default before switching models.

Not a gap: the Anthropic tool and system breakpoints are at the end of fixed content, as recommended [A1]. Prompts are far above the minimum length (about 15,000 tokens of tools and system). The moving breakpoint follows the documented pattern. The Responses codec already gets `encrypted_content` with `store: false` by default [O2].

32	
33	**Append-only record, separate from visibility.** Each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent to the model. A request renders that record plus the new items. No item is rewritten, dropped or re-derived; what the model should still see is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. Source cited: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages doc (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`): a cleared message stays in the array but renders nothing, must be re-sent verbatim, and rebuilding or dropping it counts as an edit to an earlier message that fails the thinking check and breaks the cache.

38	|---|---|---|
39	| Operator, standing | Anthropic top-level `system`; Responses `instructions` | Standing prompt and tools, written once per chat, never changed |
